residue.text: N1 is already recognized but remains dashboard-pending through boundary 3; clearing at boundary 4 is fixed. Delay origin is unknown. A repeated N1 receipt wastes a delivery slot; this anomaly establishes no broader defect.

No later-window observations, empirical comparison, global optimality proof, or additional channels are supplied. Later adaptation is unobserved and no new demand occurs now. A present receipt-dose harm test cannot replace a later-demand probe; causal identification remains conditional.

summary.text: Fixed goal: eight registrations and eight distinct recognitions by boundary 9 within six dispatcher actions. Candidate: register N3,N4,N5,N6,N7,N8 at ticks 0,1,2,3,4,5; request individuals N2,N3,N4 at ticks 0,1,2, bulk at tick 4 for N5,N6, then individuals N7,N8 at ticks 5,6. Predicted deliveries occur at 1,2,3,5,6,7,8; N1 recognition already exists. This is a finite-model prediction, not execution.

Exogenous account: later status-query demand changes independently of receipt practice. Tool-induced account: repeated bulk receipts teach senders to expect frequent traffic and cause later separate queries. Both concern later demand; the supplied return link is speculation, not an observation.

Proposed intervention suppresses redundant sender-visible receipts using recognition-ledger-guided individual/batched requests. Closest rival: routine bulk practice. Proposed separating probe compares later status-query arrivals after equal initial demand and successful recognition. Sham/control performs the same ledger review while retaining usual sender-visible repetition. Screen schedules using existing ledgers; a control missing eight recognitions is inadmissible. Later observation and a success-preserving sham are unestablished, so this probe remains conditional.

With demonstrated receipt contrast and comparable exposure, the exogenous account predicts no systematic later-demand reduction after suppression; the tool-induced account predicts fewer later queries. Unchanged later demand defeats the proposed positive return effect. Lower later demand challenges strict exogeneity but does not prove causality without controlling other later changes.

Actor burden remains one registration clerk, one dispatcher with six action units, automatic FIFO processing, and readable ledgers. Track registrations, distinct recognitions, actions, failures, duplicates, eligibility, and pending display separately. Future sender query burden remains hypothetical.
